correctness.rationale: Boolean-lattice covers encode rank. Directed-path counts to each uniquely marked vertex distinguish all atom marker-membership profiles. In an equitable stable colouring each colour cell has identical directed walk counts to every marked singleton cell. The incoming neighbours of a rank-k vertex are its k one-atom deletions, whose known profile vectors sum to (k-1) times the vertex profile; induction from atoms therefore recovers the full profile in at most 2n-2 rounds. Coordinate permutations preserve markers exactly when they stay in membership-pattern regions, and their orbits are precisely these profiles. Direct vertex-level tests verified 2047 configurations up to n=7.

value.rationale: The result states exact orbit recovery for every number and arrangement of individually marked Boolean elements using only local counting in the cover digraph, plus closed formulas for orbit counts and sizes. It distinguishes a nontrivial exponential pattern geometry that the unmarked rank partition does not encode; the structural result is genuinely uniform rather than an isolated finite experiment.
